The coordinator only needs to care about the state transition from one state to another state. That `stat`e itself can be anything, as long as the coordinator can check the transition. So something like this could be an interface: ``` fn default_state() -> State fn check_state_transition(current_state : State, new_state : State, witness : Witness) -> bool``` With that in mind, we can probably remove the part where the coordinator contributes first before launching the server, or maybe I'm misinterpretting that part? (re @Recmo: Here's the sequencer we are working on: https://github.com/recmo/kzg-ceremony-coordinator) <kevaundray> Were there any questions/concerns on the rest API document, re authorisation or endpoints, etc? Hi I took closer look on the lobby style, and would like to add a small step right before let user get in the lobby. my main concern is if the lobby reaches max. size, we should still allow user to sign in. the thinking is in the official version, i'm planning to have "my account" page where user can view their attestation and share on social. also it will feel softer on the flow, instead of reject them right away. the flow i'm thinking: - user sign in (doesn't matter if lobby reaches max. limit) - user choose to contribute, or user choose to see my account -- user choose to contribute, then - user see the lobby status (whether its full or not full) -- user see lobby has free slot - input random secret - get in lobby ((the rest is the same from Kev's doc) see flow chart here: https://www.figma.com/file/oRGtI6kDrhCBgfeuF6DyPg?node-id=302:471#262481862 <kevaundray> > <kevaundray> To clarify, currently when a user logs in, they are placed into the lobby immediately and will need to start periodically pinging the coordinator for a spot to contribute. This means that a user cannot login if the lobby is full. With this change, a user can login and be in a third state where they are not in the lobby, and as such they are not under pressure to start pinging the coordinator for a spot to contribute. Also since users are not immediately placed into the lobby, any amount of users can login even if the lobby is full (re @kzg_ceremony_bot: <Chiali> Hi I took closer look on the lobby style, and would like to add a small step right before let user get in the lobby. my main concern is if the lobby reaches max. size, we should still allow user to sign in. the thinking is in the official version, i'm planning to have "my account" page where user can view their attestation and share on social. also it will feel softer on the flow, instead of reject them right away. the flow i'm thinking: - user sign in (doesn't matter if lobby reaches max. limit) - user choose to contribute, or user choose to see my account -- user choose to contribute, then - user see the lobby status (whether its full or not full) -- user see lobby has free slot - input random secret - get in lobby ((the rest is the same from Kev's doc) see flow chart here: https://www.figma.com/file/oRGtI6kDrhCBgfeuF6DyPg?node-id=302:471#262481862 https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/974028042257190933/1017518833675800729/unknown.png) Thank you Kev for adding up this detail 🙂 <kevaundray> I don't have strong opinions on either approach tbh. The change would entail adding a new endpoint /lobby/join and the coordinator would need to keep a separate list of users who are not in the lobby but are signed in. @CarlBeek and @trent_vanepps what were your thoughts?

excerpts.content:
<kevaundray> > <kevaundray>  Skimmed the code, nice to see you also using axum 🙂 

One suggestion I'd say is to not directly have any curve related code in the coordinator crate like arb_fr. The coordinator only needs to care about the state transition from one state to another state. That `stat`e itself can be anything, as long as the coordinator can check the transition.


So something like this could be an interface:

```

fn default_state() -> State
fn check_state_transition(current_state : State, new_state : State, witness : Witness) -> bool```



With that in mind, we can probably remove the part where the coordinator contributes first before launching the server, or maybe I'm misinterpretting that part? (re @Recmo: Here's the sequencer we are working on: https://github.com/recmo/kzg-ceremony-coordinator)

Hi I took closer look on the lobby style, and would like to add a small step right before let user get in the lobby.
my main concern is if the lobby reaches max. size, we should still allow user to sign in.
the thinking is in the official version, i'm planning to have "my account" page where user can view their attestation and share on social.
also it will feel softer on the flow, instead of reject them right away.

the flow i'm thinking:
- user sign in (doesn't matter if lobby reaches max. limit)
- user choose to contribute, or user choose to see my account
-- user choose to contribute, then - user see the lobby status (whether its full or not full)
-- user see lobby has free slot - input random secret - get in lobby
((the rest is the same from Kev's doc)
see flow chart here: https://www.figma.com/file/oRGtI6kDrhCBgfeuF6DyPg?node-id=302:471#262481862
